_comment: Monolith data-driven level layouts (Goldenstone roadmap, Phase 2).
A layout is DATA: this file is the source of truth for what gets placed, not C++.
Built-ins live here (Plugins/Monolith/Config/MonolithLevelLayouts.json).
Your own layouts go in Plugins/Monolith/Saved/Monolith/LevelLayouts/*.json —
same shape, and a layout id defined there overrides a built-in of the same name.
Shape:
layouts.<layout_id>.description   human text
layouts.<layout_id>.folder        outliner folder (default Monolith/Layouts/<layout_id>)
layouts.<layout_id>.origin        [x,y,z] offset added to every entry
layouts.<layout_id>.entries[]     one placed actor each
Entry:
id      REQUIRED, unique inside the layout. This is the identity: re-applying
the layout finds the actor tagged Monolith.LayoutEntry:<id> instead of
spawning a second one.
kind    actor | light | atmosphere | volume. Selects which existing action
places it: mesh.spawn_actor / mesh.place_light / mesh.spawn_atmosphere
/ mesh.spawn_volume.
Every other key is forwarded to that action verbatim, so anything those
actions accept works here (preset, properties, extent, mobility, ...).
'class' is the layout spelling of spawn_actor's 'class_or_mesh'.
'name' / 'label' set the actor label (default '<layout_id>.<entry_id>').
Free-form properties, per kind (all validated before anything is placed):
light       properties           = UPROPERTYs on the light component
atmosphere  properties           = fields of the atmosphere settings struct
actor       properties           = UPROPERTYs on the ACTOR
component_properties = UPROPERTYs on its ROOT COMPONENT
volume      properties           = spawn_volume's curated keys only
(pain: damage_per_sec/pain_causing, audio: priority,
post_process: unbound/blend_radius/blend_weight/priority)
Apply with mesh.apply_level_layout, inspect with mesh.describe_level_layout,
undo with mesh.remove_level_layout, look at the result with editor.capture_viewport.

demo_lit_room.description: Three-walled 10x10m grey-box room with a golden-hour sun, sky light, two warm practicals, a window rect light, morning haze, sky atmosphere, a cinematic grade, a movable pedestal that sets UPROPERTYs on both the actor and its component, and a doorway trigger volume. Reference layout: shows geometry, lights, atmosphere, free-form properties and volumes composing in one document, all values coming from named presets.

three_point_studio.description: Pure lighting layout — no geometry. Classic key / fill / rim rect-light rig plus an overcast sky light for ambient. Drop it on top of whatever is already in the level. Shows a preset being composed with an explicit property override (the fill is the softbox preset dimmed through 'properties').
